Load 29: the view origin, column $05 and row $00 in characters. The little-endian address $A5E6 of this load’s entity records. $1863 copies it into the pointer at $E2–$E3.

The initial entity-slot limit is 5. $186D copies it to $4DBA, which bounds the slots that entity records fill: the initializer at $1863 loads records into slots 1 to 5 ($18CB). A 256-byte lookup indexed by screen character value: entry N is the colour-RAM byte for character N. After $6D17 draws the 20-by-10 metatile map window, it jumps to $6F3E, whose loop at $6F59–$6F5F reads each character of that screen buffer and writes the corresponding table byte to colour RAM, 39 columns by 20 rows from $D8C8. The view-shift routines read the table the same way for the column or row a scroll exposes: $30E1 for the right column, $319C for the left column, $3256 for the bottom row and $3314 for the top row. The visual-selector screens take their colours from the tables at $7F9E/$7FA5 instead, through $70ED. The table continues across $8000.
Continuation of the character-to-colour lookup beginning at $7FCF; this byte is entry $31 of that table, and entries continue through $80CE.

A 256-byte attribute table indexed by the map's metatile value. The player's downward check tests bits 0–1 at $0C57 and, for the next column, at $0C7A; the player's horizontal checks at $0EB8 and $1051 test bit 1 when clipping the player against a tile. For entities, the downward scan at $450C tests bits 0–1 at $4532 and $4542, and the horizontal test at $460C reads four attributes through $4632 (at $464C), keeping bit 1 of the first two and bit 0 of the last two.

A 256-byte table of top-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D4D writes the selected code to the first cell of a two-by-two screen block. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of top-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D53 writes the selected code to the cell to the right of the first cell. A 256-byte table of bottom-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D5A writes the selected code to one 40-character screen row below the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and ($58) at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2CF1 (scrolling right) and $2DE6 (left), for a column of right halves, and at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

Load 29: low bytes for pointer entries 14–77 of the 81-entry split table. Paired with the high table, these encode $8911 through $94E1 in 48-byte steps modulo 65536, the row stride at $7F4A. They lie beyond the map’s 14 rows, the count at $7F4C. The window draw at $6D30 and the scroll readers at $2CD4, $2DC9, $2EC2 and $2F9D index by the view’s rows, which the scroll check at $0CCC keeps within the map. The hero’s tile checks index the table by his row $6F3D ($0EA7, $1041, $6E77) or that row plus one ($0C47, $0C69, $6E8D); $6F3D reaches 14 when the view is at the bottom of the map and the hero at his lowest screen position $E1 ($0CFC), so entries 14 and 15 can be read, and no hero check reaches entries 16–77. The entity collision checks at $451D and $4638 index the table by an entity’s tile row from $71DB, plus one to three, with no bound of their own.

Load 29: characters $80–$BC of the map's character set, the eight-page copy that starts at $8911 (the source address at $7F41/$7F42), 488 bytes. $717C copies them to $D400–$D5E7. The map's tiles draw characters $82–$83, $8E and $9D–$AC.

Load 29 update entry: load X from $4DBD and write $10, the round number, to $4DCB,X. It jumps to $0732, which loads the next part, when column $6F3C equals $2E; otherwise it jumps to $0200. Before that test, values of $4DB5 at least $05 are set to $04. Load 29 trigger record 1 of 1: initial bytes $FF, $FF, $FF, $FF, $00, $00. $7979 copies the fields to the column, row, remaining-count, argument and callback arrays; the initial callback address is $0000. $48BF compares the stored column and row with the view tile, checks and decrements the count, then dispatches through the callback. Its callback address $0000 is not code in the load; no code other than the dispatcher's DEC at $48E4 changes the count.

Load 29 stage-object record 1 of 2: bytes $05, $08, $01, $01, $00, $00, $00, $00, $00, $00, $40, $8F, $2F, $30, $3C, $3D. $4655 copies bytes 0–11 to the twelve arrays at $4747–$4789 (bytes 0–3 are the column, row, screen selector and state) and bytes 12–15 to $7D–$80, then calls $46D6, which writes those four map cells as the two-by-two block at columns $05–$06 of rows $07–$08; when the state byte is negative it first replaces them with $7F6D–$7F70, or $7F71–$7F74 when $7A is nonzero. When the main loop’s call of $478F at $042C finds the hero at column $05, row $08 ($6F3C/$6F3D) with $527D equal to $0F, the input byte $75 zero and the state not negative, $479C lowers the state ($01 at the start) by 2, passes byte 2, $01, in X to $7119 at $47F5, which draws the screen of visual selector 1, and calls the callback $8F40 from bytes 10 and 11 through the JSR at $47FC; if the state is then negative, $46D6 rewrites the cells.

Load 29 stage-object record 2 of 2: bytes $05, $08, $02, $02, $15, $16, $4A, $00, $00, $00, $8D, $90, $2B, $2C, $2D, $2E. $4655 copies bytes 0–11 to the twelve arrays at $4747–$4789 (bytes 0–3 are the column, row, screen selector and state) and bytes 12–15 to $7D–$80, then calls $46D6, which writes those four map cells as the two-by-two block at columns $05–$06 of rows $07–$08; when the state byte is negative it first replaces them with $7F6D–$7F70, or $7F71–$7F74 when $7A is nonzero. When the main loop’s call of $478F at $042C finds the hero at column $05, row $08 ($6F3C/$6F3D) with $527D equal to $0F, the input byte $75 zero and the state not negative, $479C lowers the state ($02 at the start) by 2, passes byte 2, $02, in X to $7119 at $47F5, which draws the screen of visual selector 2, and calls the callback $908D from bytes 10 and 11 through the JSR at $47FC; if the state is then negative, $46D6 rewrites the cells.

Load 29: a quest step; stage object record 1 at $8F20 names it in its bytes 11 and 12. It reads the selected player's progress number, bits 0–2 of $4DE2,Y. Unless it is 3, it passes message number $16 and then 0 to $77E2. When it is 3, it sets it to 4, shows the messages at $8FF2, $9028 and $9062 (the first begins “Oh! Welcome here.”) through $77E0, passes 0 to the message routine, copies the 72 bytes at $8FAA to $CCD0–$CD17, characters $9A–$A2, and puts the nine codes at $8FA1 into three rows of the status panel at $5023, $5038 and $504D. The map's eight-page character copy, which starts at $8911, also takes $8F40–$8FA0 to $D62F–$D68F as characters $C5–$D1.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “Oh! Welcome here.” / “You are really” / “brave. I award you[$60]”, then the control byte $FF. [$60] is glyph $60, the downward-pointing triangle that ends a page. The instruction sequence at $8F62 loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B; for $FF it shows the message on the status panel through two calls of $370B, waits for Fire at $6DDE, which blinks the triangle, and then sets the countdown to 5, so the message stays for five more panel updates.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “the emblem for your” / “courage. The Great” / “Dragon is in the[$60]”, then the control byte $FF. [$60] is glyph $60, the downward-pointing triangle that ends a page. The instruction sequence at $8F69 loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B; for $FF it shows the message on the status panel through two calls of $370B, waits for Fire at $6DDE, which blinks the triangle, and then sets the countdown to 5, so the message stays for five more panel updates.

Load 29: $9061 is the control byte $FF of the message at $9028, three zero-terminated glyph lines “the emblem for your” / “courage. The Great” / “Dragon is in the[$60]”. $8F69 loads its address in X/Y and calls $77E0. $77E2 stores the control byte $FF in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel waits for Fire with the blinking prompt marker $60 and then shows the message for 5 more of its updates. $717C also copies it to $D750, as byte 0 of character $EA of the map's eight-page character copy, which starts at $8911 (the source address at $7F41/$7F42).

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “Monster Castle.” / “Is sure to beat him!” / “[$60]”, then the control byte $FF. [$60] is glyph $60, the downward-pointing triangle that ends a page. The instruction sequence at $8F70 loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B; for $FF it shows the message on the status panel through two calls of $370B, waits for Fire at $6DDE, which blinks the triangle, and then sets the countdown to 5, so the message stays for five more panel updates.

Two jump entries: $908A enters the price setup at $9090, and $908D jumps to the item-pair setup at $91B0. Load 29’s stage record 2 at $8F30 names $908D as its callback; no record or instruction in load 29 or in the resident part names $908A. The map’s eight-page character copy, which starts at $8911, also takes these six bytes, to $D779–$D77E.

Write $46 plus 1 modulo 256 to the high address byte at $93EF of the digit store at $93ED and to the layout gate at $9439, set sound state $2C15 to 2, and use stage index $7B to format fields $4783,X and $4789,X through $90F3 with Y=$9B and Y=$AF as the screen offsets of their last digits.
Use selected-player index $4DBD. If $4DC7,Y is nonzero, or if $4DC9,Y is at least stage field $4789,X under an unsigned byte comparison, go to $90DE. Otherwise inspect stage field $4753,X.

Load 29: the not-enough-gold message: load message pointer $9528 in X/Y and jump to the message call at $937A. The code falls in here from $90C7 when the record's $4753,X is 3, and the BEQ at $90D2 branches here when bit 0 of $4753,X is clear. The map's character copy, which starts at $8911, also takes $90C9–$90CF to $D7B8–$D7BE as character $F7.

Reached when stage field $4753,X is not 3: test its bit 0. A clear bit selects message $9528; a set bit calls $93C1, which stores $FF in $4753,X, then selects message $9512 and jumps to the message call at $937A.

Reached from the balance check when the gold covers stage field $4789,X. Test bit 0 of stage field $4753,X: clear selects message $94D4, set selects $94BD. Both jump to $926D, which shows the message and starts the choice loop.

Save X in the immediate operand at $911B and Y in the one at $9116, call $36E9 to split A into nibbles plus one, clear the first two bytes at $9434, and write the tens and units codes to the next two bytes. A tens code of 1 is written as zero. Restore Y, call $93DB, restore X and return.

The flags come from the selection byte $943A, loaded at $9306 before the only jump here ($9309, taken when the layout gate $9439 is nonzero): negative ($FF, left) enters the first-price balance check at $914F; zero selects message $94FB at $919D; otherwise (1, right) take the second-price path at $9121.

Reached from $911D when the shop selection byte is 1. Load X from $7B and call $78D1 with stage field $4789,X, record byte 9, the second price: $78D1 subtracts it in packed decimal from the selected player’s gold and restores the gold if that borrows. Reload X and read callback high byte $4771,X. If nonzero, patch the JSR operand at $913F from $476B/$4771 (record bytes 4 and 5), clear the high byte in the stage record so that the callback runs only once, and call the patched target; then use A=4 at $9192, which adds it to the life meter. If zero, enter the message path at $9146, which shows message $9569 and then does the same with A=4. No stage record in load 29 names this shop’s entry $908A (JMP $9090), so this code does not run in load 29.

Second-price fallback: load X/Y with message $9569 (“Nice and cold, / is'nt it?”, control byte $10, so the panel shows it for 16 updates), set A=4 and jump to $918D, which calls $77E0, pulls A and adds 4 to the selected player's life meter through $77A9. $912E branches here when the callback high byte $4771,X (record byte 5) is zero, after $78D1 has taken the second price, record byte 9, from the gold; the high byte is cleared once that record's callback has run. Load 29 never runs it: the purchase gate takes the price paths only when the layout gate $9439 is nonzero, and no stage-object record in load 29 names the price set-up $908A; its record 2 names only the item-pair set-up $908D, which stores zero in the gate.

If selected-player high balance $4DC7,Y is zero and low balance $4DC9,Y is less than stage field $4783,X under an unsigned byte comparison, jump to $928D. Otherwise continue to the first-price payment at $9164.

Reached from the balance check at $914F, which the selection path sends here when the shop selection byte is $FF and lets through when the selected player’s gold covers the first price. Call $78D1 with stage field $4783,X, record byte 8, the first price, which $78D1 subtracts in packed decimal from the gold, and reload the stage index. If callback high byte $477D,X is nonzero, patch the JSR operand at $9180 from $4777/$477D (record bytes 6 and 7), clear that high byte so that the callback runs only once, and call the target; then use A=8 at $9192, which adds it to the life meter. Otherwise enter the message path at $9187, which shows message $9584 and then does the same with A=8. No stage record in load 29 names this shop’s entry $908A (JMP $9090), so this code does not run in load 29.

First-price fallback: load X/Y with message $9584 (“How do you like / the cocktail?”, control byte $10, so the panel shows it for 16 updates), set A=8 and fall into $918D, which calls $77E0, pulls A and adds 8 to the selected player's life meter through $77A9. $916F branches here when the callback high byte $477D,X (record byte 7) is zero, after $78D1 has taken the first price, record byte 8, from the gold; the high byte is cleared once that record's callback has run. Load 29 never runs it: the purchase gate takes the price paths only when the layout gate $9439 is nonzero, and no stage-object record in load 29 names the price set-up $908A; its record 2 names only the item-pair set-up $908D, which stores zero in the gate.

Push A, call $77E0 with the message pointer in X/Y and pull A, then continue at $9192, which adds A to the player’s meter through $77A9. The second-price fallback jumps here from $914C with A=4 and message $9569; the first-price fallback falls in from $9187 with A=8 and message $9584.

Call $77A9 with A=4 or A=8, reload stage index, decrement $4753,X and jump to $937D. The two price paths jump here, $9143 with A=4 and $9184 with A=8, after paying. $77A9 adds A to the selected player’s life meter $4DCD,Y, capped at the limit $4DCF,Y; $937D calls $3C2A and $370B until the message countdown $4D6B is zero and returns. No stage record in load 29 names this shop’s entry, so the code does not run in load 29.
Load X/Y with message pointer $94FB and jump to the message call at $937A. $911F branches here when the selection byte read at $9306 is zero.

Reload stage index, decrement $4753,X, load message pointer $9545 in X/Y and jump to the message call at $937A. The only jump here is from the timeout path at $92B2, taken when the layout gate $9439 is nonzero.
Store zero at the layout gate $9439, set sound state $2C15 to 2, and set $4D69 to 7. Reload stage index from $7B and continue to the item-pair selection at $91C1. The jump entry at $908D leads here.

Read $476B,X. If nonzero, pass it and $4771,X separately through the conditional-item resolver at $9389; store the returned values at $943F/$9440, then jump to $91FE. If zero, branch to the implicit pair at $91DA.

Use $4771,X, byte 5 of the stage-object record selected by $7B, as Y. Clear carry, add the selected player $4DBD (0 or 1) and then $D5, and store the sum as the low byte of the LDA at $91EE; store $4D plus the carry as its high byte. Load 29 never runs it: the one record that names the shop's item-pair entry at $908D, record 2 at $8F30 (items $15 and $16), gives a nonzero byte 4, so the BEQ at $91C6 never branches here.

Read the absolute address patched by $91E4 and $91EB, $4DD5 plus stage field $4771,X plus the selected player index; clear carry and add $9441,Y, where Y is that stage field. Store the result at $943F, then store that result plus one modulo 256 at $9440. Continue at $91FE.

Load the second item's number from $9440, multiply it by eight modulo 256 and read the picture-routine address at offsets 2 and 3 of its row in the 24-row item table at $9790. Patch the JSR operand at $9214/$9215. Load 29's shop records give second items 22 here, all rows of the table: record 2 at $8F30 gives items $15 and $16.

Multiply A, the second item's number that $91FE loads from $9440, by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's picture-routine address at $9792,Y and $9793,Y (row offsets 2 and 3) into the operand of the JSR at $9213, which calls it with A=$E4. Load 29's shop records give items 22 here, all rows of the 24-row item table at $9790.
Call the patched target with A=$E4. Then read the first item byte at $943F, multiply it by eight modulo 256 and patch the JSR operand at $922C/$922D from the same pointer table.

Multiply A, the first item's number that $9216 loads from $943F, by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's picture-routine address at $9792,Y and $9793,Y (row offsets 2 and 3) into the operand of the JSR at $922B, which calls it with A=$D0. Load 29's shop records give items 21 here, all rows of the 24-row item table at $9790.
Call the second patched target with A=$D0, then set the temporary row counter at $978F to 3 and begin filling colour RAM.

For each of three rows, write colour 9 to four bytes at $D8F8,Y and four at $D90C,Y. Y starts at zero and advances by 40 after each row; the counter at $978F ends at zero. With I/O visible, these are colour RAM writes. The next setup continues at $924D.
Store $46 plus one modulo 256 at $93EF. Pass the first selected item at $943F to $93F6, then call $93DB with Y=$73. Repeat for the second item at $9440 with Y=$87.

Call $77E0 with the message pointer selected by the preceding path, then fall through to the mode and countdown initializer at $9270. The item-pair path loads $9446; the price path jumps here from $90E9 or $90F0 with $94D4 or $94BD.

Store 0 in the selection byte at $943A, store $DC in the countdown at $943E, and fall through to the wait path at $927A. Besides this store, only the left and right handlers write the selection byte, and they keep it among $FF, 0 and 1.

Call $3C2A, decrement the shop countdown at $943E and branch to $92AD when it becomes zero. Otherwise call $370B, $93B1 and $939E; on set carry, repeat this path. On clear carry, fall through to $928D. Starting from the initialized $DC, the countdown reaches zero on the 220th call to $3C2A, counting the calls of this loop and of the one at $928D together.
Call $3C2A, decrement $943E and branch to $92AD at zero. Otherwise call $370B, $93B1 and $3C4C, then fall through to the sampled-input choice at $929E.

Use the sampled active-low inputs: if $70 is zero, branch to the shop gate at $9301; otherwise, if $73 is zero, branch to the left handler at $92C3; otherwise, if $74 is zero, branch to the right handler at $92E1. When all three are nonzero, jump back to $928D. The preceding code calls $3C4C to sample joystick port 2; fire takes priority over left, and left over right.

Reached when the countdown at $943E reaches zero. If $9439 is nonzero, jump to $91A4. Otherwise load X from $7B, store $FF at $4753,X, load X/Y with message pointer $947B, and jump to the $77E0 call at $937A.

If the signed mode byte at $943A is negative, return to the wait path at $927A. Otherwise decrement it with eight-bit wrap. If the new value is nonzero and $9439 is zero, pass the item index at $943F to the message selector at $93C9. Call $93B1 and return to the wait path.

If the mode byte at $943A equals 1, return to the wait path at $927A. Otherwise increment it with eight-bit wrap. If the new value is nonzero and $9439 is zero, pass the item index at $9440 to the message selector at $93C9. Call $93B1 and return to the wait path.

Read the layout gate $9439; if nonzero, load the selection byte $943A and jump to $911D. Otherwise load X from $7B and read $943A. If nonzero, branch to the purchase index choice at $932A, preserving the negative flag from that read. If zero, inspect $4753,X: a negative value or a clear bit 1 selects message pointer $94A3; a nonnegative value with bit 1 set selects $948C. Both paths jump to the $77E0 message call. $9439 is $46 plus one on the price path ($9096) and zero on the item-pair path ($91B2).
Choose an item index using the incoming negative flag: load $943F when it is set, or $9440 when clear, then enter the price selector at $9335. The path at $9301 supplies that flag from $943A.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts, use the result as Y, and copy the item row's price at $9790,Y and $9791,Y (row offsets 0 and 1) to $7D/$7E. Call $7901, which subtracts the packed-decimal amount from the selected player’s gold, restores it on insufficient funds, returns carry set on success and clears decimal mode. The code at $932A passes the first item's number from $943F when the selection byte is negative, or the second item's from $9440. Load 29's shop records give items 21 and 22 here, all rows of the 24-row item table at $9790.

After the $7901 price subtraction, jump to $927A on clear carry. On set carry, load X from $7B and decrement $4753,X with eight-bit wrap. Read $943A; if negative select the item index at $943F, otherwise select $9440. Push it and continue to the offset-4 routine-pointer selector at $935F.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's purchase-routine address at $9794,Y and $9795,Y (row offsets 4 and 5) into the operand of the JSR at $9373, which calls it with the item number plus 1 in A. A is the bought item's number, pushed by the code before: the first item from $943F when the selection byte is negative, otherwise the second from $9440. Load 29's shop records give items 21 and 22 here, all rows of the 24-row item table at $9790.

Pull the selected item index, clear carry, add 1 in binary mode and call the JSR whose operand was patched by the selector. Load X/Y with $9468 and call $77E0, then call $3C2A and $370B repeatedly while $4D6B is nonzero. Return once it is zero.
Load 29: return A unchanged unless it equals $13. For $13, inspect bit $10 of the selected player’s flags: return $14 when set, or $13 when clear. The shop item-pair path uses this resolver.

Load 29: call the input sampler at $3C4C and return carry set if any of $73, $74 or $70 is zero, carry clear if all are nonzero. The sampler reads joystick port 2 active-low, so carry is set while the stick is pushed left or right or fire is pressed.

Load 29: with decimal mode clear, add one to the selection byte at $943A, use the wrapped result as an index into $943B, and pass that position in X and $82 in Y to $719E. The selection byte stays among $FF, 0 and 1, so the index is 0 to 2.
Load X from $7B, store $FF at $4753,X and return. The insufficient-gold path calls it at $90D4, and the item effects at $9853, $9859, $985F, $9865, $986E, $987A and $9897 tail-call it.

Multiply A, an item's number, by 8 using three eight-bit shifts, clear carry, add 6 and use the eight-bit result as X. Read the high byte from $9791,X into Y and the low byte from $9790,X into X, the message pointer at offsets 6 and 7 of the item's row in the 24-row item table at $9790, then jump to $77E0. Entry $77E0 loads A=0, so the message routine uses X/Y as a direct pointer. The selection paths call this routine at $92D8 with the first item's number from $943F and at $92F8 with the second's from $9440. Load 29's shop records give items 21 and 22 here, all rows of the table: record 2 at $8F30 gives items $15 and $16.

Load 29: process four price-display bytes at $9434 in reverse order. Leave zero unchanged; add $F5 to each nonzero byte with eight-bit wrap and decimal mode clear. Call the digit writer at $93ED with successive Y positions, decrementing Y after each call.

Load 29: store A at offset Y of the page after $46, through STA $FF00,Y. $9093 and $9250 each set its high byte $93EF to $46 plus one, $C1 or $C5, since $46 holds the screen page $C0 or $C4; the load holds $FF there. Then write colour 1 to $D900,Y, the matching colour RAM, and return. Called from $93E5. Colour RAM requires I/O visible.

Load 29: multiply item ID A by eight with eight-bit wrap, split the two packed bytes from the item table at $9790 into four nibble-plus-one values at $9434, and replace consecutive leading ones with zero. $9256 and $9261 pass the first and second items on offer, which load 29's shop records make 21 and 22, all rows of the 24-row table, and every price in those rows is packed decimal, so each value is a digit plus one, 1 to 10.

Load 29: four working price-display bytes. The item-price formatter at $93F6 and the stage-price formatter at $90F3 write them, and the drawing loop at $93DB reads them in reverse, from $9437 down to $9434, passing each to the digit writer at $93ED.

Load 29: one byte, $AB in the load, between the four price-display cells at $9434–$9437 and the layout gate at $9439. No instruction in load 29 or in the resident part names it, and the indexed accesses to $9434 at $93DD, $9424 and $942B keep X between 0 and 3, so none reaches it.
Load 29: mutable shop layout gate. Timeout, selection and purchase code read this byte to choose alternate paths.
Load 29: mutable shop selection byte. The input loop initializes it to zero, left and right paths update it, and the cursor helper indexes the position table using this value plus one.

Load 29: three cursor-position bytes, $5F, $B4 and $FF, for selections $FF, 0 and 1: the cursor helper at $93B1 reads them at $93BA with the selection byte plus one as index, and passes the byte in X to $719E. No instruction writes them.
Load 29: mutable shop timeout. The input loop initializes it to $DC and decrements it during both input-release and polling paths.

Load 29: mutable first item ID. $91CB or $91F5 stores it; the item drawing at $9216, the price label at $9253, the left-selection description at $92D5 and the purchase paths at $9332 and $935B read it.

Load 29: mutable second item ID. $91D4 or $91FB stores it; the item drawing at $91FE, the price label at $925E, the right-selection description at $92F5 and the purchase paths at $932C and $9355 read it.

Load 29: five item-index offsets, $00, $00, $0D, $00 and $06, at $9441–$9445. ADC $9441,Y at $91F2 adds the offset selected by Y, stage field $4771,X, to the player-state value and stores the first item ID; the following addition of one supplies the second ID. Load 29’s only shop record, record 2 at $8F30, holds the explicit pair $15 and $16 in $476B/$4771, so this load never takes the implicit path that reads these bytes.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “Welcome!” / “May I help you?” / “”, then the control byte $20. The instruction sequence at $9269 loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B, so the status panel shows the message for 32 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “” / “Thank you.” / “”, then the control byte $10. The instruction sequence at $9376 loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B, so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 29, shop message 3: three zero-terminated fields "" / "      Closed." / "", followed by control byte $18. The shop timeout at $92AD, when the layout gate $9439 is zero, stores $FF in stage field $4753,X and loads this address in X/Y at $92BC, then jumps to the $77E0 call at $937A. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 24 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 29, shop message 4: three zero-terminated fields "" / " Please come again." / "", followed by control byte $10.
